prompt: Complete a static tile method that returns a new BufferedImage repeating a source image in a cols-by-rows grid, without modifying the source.
explanation: A BufferedImage is just an in-memory raster you can both read and draw on: createGraphics() hands back a Graphics2D whose target is the image itself, and drawImage stamps the source at any offset. Two nested loops place one copy per grid cell at (c * srcWidth, r * srcHeight). Disposing the graphics in a finally block releases its resources, and because drawing only reads from src, the source image is left untouched -- which the tests verify.
hints: Create the output first: new BufferedImage(src.getWidth() * cols, src.getHeight() * rows, BufferedImage.TYPE_INT_RGB).
out.createGraphics() gives a Graphics2D that draws INTO the new image; dispose it in a finally block.
Nested loops over rows and cols: drawImage(src, c * src.getWidth(), r * src.getHeight(), null).
